  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.
3. **Never-again**: pin the harbor version the workflow installs (or at least floor+ceiling), and/or add a cheap setup-only smoke (`tasks=<smoke>`, attempts=1) to CI so the harbor path is exercised on bench/** changes instead of drifting silently.
4. After merge: re-dispatch TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding full run (provider=custom, provider-config kimi-for-coding 200k/16k, attempts=1, confirm-full-run=true, progress-extension=true).

## Notes

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /

  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.
3. **Never-again**: pin the harbor version the workflow installs (or at least floor+ceiling), and/or add a cheap setup-only smoke (`tasks=<smoke>`, attempts=1) to CI so the harbor path is exercised on bench/** changes instead of drifting silently.
4. After merge: re-dispatch TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding full run (provider=custom, provider-config kimi-for-coding 200k/16k, attempts=1, confirm-full-run=true, progress-extension=true).

## Notes

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /

  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.
3. **Never-again**: pin the harbor version the workflow installs (or at least floor+ceiling), and/or add a cheap setup-only smoke (`tasks=<smoke>`, attempts=1) to CI so the harbor path is exercised on bench/** changes instead of drifting silently.
4. After merge: re-dispatch TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding full run (provider=custom, provider-config kimi-for-coding 200k/16k, attempts=1, confirm-full-run=true, progress-extension=true).

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

"""Unit tests for the bench agent-timeout ladder (issue #1122).

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench
The adapter-level tests skip when terminal_bench / harbor is not installed;
the ladder tests run anywhere (pure stdlib shared module).
"""
import asyncio
import base64
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import types
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import fa_agent_timeout
from fa_agent_timeout import ProgressLadder, TimeoutKnobs, audit_dict

def _importable(name: str) -> bool:
    # find_spec is not enough: with bench/terminal_bench on sys.path (as
    # unittest discover does), find_spec("terminal_bench") matches the
    # DIRECTORY itself as a namespace package and false-positives.
    try:
        module = importlib.import_module(name)
    except ImportError:
        return False
    # test_progress_watch_adapter installs a stdlib stub package under the
    # same name (so its ITs run where terminal-bench is not installed);
    # a stub is not the real dependency.
    return not getattr(module, "__fa_tb_stub__", False)


TB_AVAILABLE = _importable("terminal_bench.agents.base_agent")
HARBOR_AVAILABLE = _importable("harbor")

KNOB_NAMES = (
    "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC",
    "FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION",
    "FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC",
    "FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER",
)


def clean_env(**overrides):
    env = {name: value for name, value in os.environ.items() if name not in KNOB_NAMES}
    env.update(overrides)
    return env


def _dart_duration_seconds(declaration: str) -> float:
    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

    Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`,
    `Duration(minutes: 5)`, `Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)`,
    `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the coupling REG (gh-1430) feeds it
    the `providerStreamIdleTimeout` line from the Dart source, and the
    parse must survive a benign unit change there.
    """
    body = declaration[declaration.index("(") + 1 : declaration.rindex(")")]
    factors = {
        "milliseconds": 0.001,
        "seconds": 1.0,
        "minutes": 60.0,
        "hours": 3600.0,
    }
    total = 0.0

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.
3. **Never-again**: pin the harbor version the workflow installs (or at least floor+ceiling), and/or add a cheap setup-only smoke (`tasks=<smoke>`, attempts=1) to CI so the harbor path is exercised on bench/** changes instead of drifting silently.
4. After merge: re-dispatch TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding full run (provider=custom, provider-config kimi-for-coding 200k/16k, attempts=1, confirm-full-run=true, progress-extension=true).

## Notes

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /

  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.
3. **Never-again**: pin the harbor version the workflow installs (or at least floor+ceiling), and/or add a cheap setup-only smoke (`tasks=<smoke>`, attempts=1) to CI so the harbor path is exercised on bench/** changes instead of drifting silently.
4. After merge: re-dispatch TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding full run (provider=custom, provider-config kimi-for-coding 200k/16k, attempts=1, confirm-full-run=true, progress-extension=true).

## Notes

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.
3. **Never-again**: pin the harbor version the workflow installs (or at least floor+ceiling), and/or add a cheap setup-only smoke (`tasks=<smoke>`, attempts=1) to CI so the harbor path is exercised on bench/** changes instead of drifting silently.
4. After merge: re-dispatch TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding full run (provider=custom, provider-config kimi-for-coding 200k/16k, attempts=1, confirm-full-run=true, progress-extension=true).

## Notes

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

blocks.text:
"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.
3. **Never-again**: pin the harbor version the workflow installs (or at least floor+ceiling), and/or add a cheap setup-only smoke (`tasks=<smoke>`, attempts=1) to CI so the harbor path is exercised on bench/** changes instead of drifting silently.
4. After merge: re-dispatch TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding full run (provider=custom, provider-config kimi-for-coding 200k/16k, attempts=1, confirm-full-run=true, progress-extension=true).

## Notes

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.
3. **Never-again**: pin the harbor version the workflow installs (or at least floor+ceiling), and/or add a cheap setup-only smoke (`tasks=<smoke>`, attempts=1) to CI so the harbor path is exercised on bench/** changes instead of drifting silently.
4. After merge: re-dispatch TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding full run (provider=custom, provider-config kimi-for-coding 200k/16k, attempts=1, confirm-full-run=true, progress-extension=true).

## Notes

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.
3. **Never-again**: pin the harbor version the workflow installs (or at least floor+ceiling), and/or add a cheap setup-only smoke (`tasks=<smoke>`, attempts=1) to CI so the harbor path is exercised on bench/** changes instead of drifting silently.
4. After merge: re-dispatch TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding full run (provider=custom, provider-config kimi-for-coding 200k/16k, attempts=1, confirm-full-run=true, progress-extension=true).

## Notes

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.

4. After merge: re-dispatch TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding full run (provider=custom, provider-config kimi-for-coding 200k/16k, attempts=1, confirm-full-run=true, progress-extension=true).

## Notes

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import shlex
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import fa_agent_timeout as _timeout

from harbor.agents.installed.base import BaseInstalledAgent
from harbor.environments.base import BaseEnvironment
from harbor.models.agent.context import AgentContext

# Shared extraction lives one level up (bench/fa_usage.py); PYTHONPATH only
# carries this dir.
_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

_VERSION = "0.1.0"

# Issue #1408 AC1 (review 5456649624): the in-container job-log dir,
# OUTSIDE the graded task workspace — same constant the terminal-bench
# adapter defines (bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py); a future relocation

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.
3. **Never-again**: pin the harbor version the workflow installs (or at least floor+ceiling), and/or add a cheap setup-only smoke (`tasks=<smoke>`, attempts=1) to CI so the harbor path is exercised on bench/** changes instead of drifting silently.
4. After merge: re-dispatch TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding full run (provider=custom, provider-config kimi-for-coding 200k/16k, attempts=1, confirm-full-run=true, progress-extension=true).

## Notes

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.
3. **Never-again**: pin the harbor version the workflow installs (or at least floor+ceiling), and/or add a cheap setup-only smoke (`tasks=<smoke>`, attempts=1) to CI so the harbor path is exercised on bench/** changes instead of drifting silently.
4. After merge: re-dispatch TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding full run (provider=custom, provider-config kimi-for-coding 200k/16k, attempts=1, confirm-full-run=true, progress-extension=true).

## Notes

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.
3. **Never-again**: pin the harbor version the workflow installs (or at least floor+ceiling), and/or add a cheap setup-only smoke (`tasks=<smoke>`, attempts=1) to CI so the harbor path is exercised on bench/** changes instead of drifting silently.
4. After merge: re-dispatch TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding full run (provider=custom, provider-config kimi-for-coding 200k/16k, attempts=1, confirm-full-run=true, progress-extension=true).

## Notes

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.
3. **Never-again**: pin the harbor version the workflow installs (or at least floor+ceiling), and/or add a cheap setup-only smoke (`tasks=<smoke>`, attempts=1) to CI so the harbor path is exercised on bench/** changes instead of drifting silently.
4. After merge: re-dispatch TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding full run (provider=custom, provider-config kimi-for-coding 200k/16k, attempts=1, confirm-full-run=true, progress-extension=true).

## Notes

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.
3. **Never-again**: pin the harbor version the workflow installs (or at least floor+ceiling), and/or add a cheap setup-only smoke (`tasks=<smoke>`, attempts=1) to CI so the harbor path is exercised on bench/** changes instead of drifting silently.
4. After merge: re-dispatch TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding full run (provider=custom, provider-config kimi-for-coding 200k/16k, attempts=1, confirm-full-run=true, progress-extension=true).

## Notes

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /

# gh-1535: [BUG] bench-harbor setup red: test_fa_agent_timeout HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation ERRORs — FaAgent() constructor drifted from harbor BaseInstalledAgent

## Description

## Symptom

The first-ever `bench-harbor.yml` dispatch on current main (run [38119283414](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38119283414), TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding, 2026-10-11) fails in the **setup job → `Unit-test bench scripts`** step before any shard starts. 6 ERRORs, all the same shape:

```
ERROR: test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract (test_fa_agent_timeout.HarborParityTest)
  File bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py, line 613, in _agent
    return self.harbor_fa.FaAgent(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / logs)
TypeError: FaAgent() takes no arguments
```

Affected: `HarborParityTest` (test_agent_command_unchanged_from_legacy_contract, test_crashed_exec_audited_as_crashed, test_natural_completion_with_extensions, test_no_knobs_takes_today_path, test_silent_agent_killed_and_classified_as_timeout) and `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest.test_harbor_provider_env_relocates_job_logs`.

## Root cause

`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` `class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent)` defines **no `__init__`** — `logs_dir` is inherited from harbor's `BaseInstalledAgent` (production code reads `self.logs_dir` at fa_agent.py:359). The tests in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` still construct `FaAgent(Path(...)/"logs")` positionally — written against an older harbor API where the constructor took the logs dir. The harbor package is installed fresh at workflow setup time, so the dependency floated under the tests.

The harbor path was **never exercised end-to-end** before this dispatch (no prior bench-harbor.yml runs in history), so the drift was invisible — bench.yml's own unit tests don't cover HarborParityTest.

## Acceptance

1. `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` HarborParity/HarnessArtifactIsolation tests construct FaAgent per the CURRENT harbor `BaseInstalledAgent` API (likely `FaAgent()` + set `agent.logs_dir = Path(...)`, or keyword form — verify against the harbor version the workflow installs; check `pip show harbor` in the setup log).
2. `python3 -m unittest bench.terminal_bench.test_fa_agent_timeout` green locally AND in the bench-harbor setup job.

4. After merge: re-dispatch TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding full run (provider=custom, provider-config kimi-for-coding 200k/16k, attempts=1, confirm-full-run=true, progress-extension=true).

- This blocks ALL bench-harbor dispatches (TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) — setup red before any LLM spend, so nothing was wasted.
- bench.yml (TB1 path) unaffected — yesterday's full kimi run (38072766471, 48/80 = 60%) was clean.
- Refs: #1316 (harbor path), #1503/#1505 (provider port that made this dispatch possible).

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —

uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):

                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

Usage:

)


def clean_env(**overrides):
    env = {name: value for name, value in os.environ.items() if name not in KNOB_NAMES}

def no_exec_session(mode):
    """A session double for never-started trials: exec_run must never be
    reached, so reaching it names the outcome that should have skipped the
    fold. Shared by the installation-failure and unknown-agent-error pins
    (gh-1209 review nit — the two doubles differed only in that name)."""

    class NoExecSession:
        class Container:
            def exec_run(self, cmd):  # pragma: no cover — must not be reached

            pass

    return NoExecSession()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Unit tests for the bench agent-timeout ladder (issue #1122).

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench
The adapter-level tests skip when terminal_bench / harbor is not installed;
the ladder tests run anywhere (pure stdlib shared module).
"""
import asyncio
import base64
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import types
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import fa_agent_timeout
from fa_agent_timeout import ProgressLadder, TimeoutKnobs, audit_dict

def _importable(name: str) -> bool:
    # find_spec is not enough: with bench/terminal_bench on sys.path (as
    # unittest discover does), find_spec("terminal_bench") matches the
    # DIRECTORY itself as a namespace package and false-positives.
    try:
        module = importlib.import_module(name)
    except ImportError:
        return False
    # test_progress_watch_adapter installs a stdlib stub package under the
    # same name (so its ITs run where terminal-bench is not installed);
    # a stub is not the real dependency.
    return not getattr(module, "__fa_tb_stub__", False)


TB_AVAILABLE = _importable("terminal_bench.agents.base_agent")
HARBOR_AVAILABLE = _importable("harbor")

KNOB_NAMES = (
    "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC",
    "FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION",
    "FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC",
    "FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER",
)


def clean_env(**overrides):
    env = {name: value for name, value in os.environ.items() if name not in KNOB_NAMES}
    env.update(overrides)
    return env


def _dart_duration_seconds(declaration: str) -> float:
    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

    Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`,
    `Duration(minutes: 5)`, `Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)`,
    `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the coupling REG (gh-1430) feeds it
    the `providerStreamIdleTimeout` line from the Dart source, and the
    parse must survive a benign unit change there.
    """

But wait: if test_fa_agent_timeout runs first, how does the stub affect it? Under `unittest discover`, ALL test modules are imported FIRST (to build the suite), THEN tests run. So during suite construction, every test_*.py is imported, including test_fa_usage.py which stubs harbor and REPLACES sys.modules["harbor.agents.installed.base"] etc. with stub modules. Then when HarborParityTest.setUpClass execs bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py, its `from harbor.agents.installed.base import BaseInstalledAgent` picks up the STUB module (already in sys.modules) → BaseInstalledAgent = bare type → FaAgent inherits object.__init__ → "FaAgent() takes no arguments"!

Module import order during discover: alphabetical. test_fa_agent_timeout imported before test_fa_usage, so HARBOR_AVAILABLE=True (real harbor at that point). Then test_fa_usage imports and stubs. Then tests execute → HarborParityTest not skipped → setUpClass loads fa_agent.py against stubbed harbor → boom.

Also why did my earlier module-path invocation pass? Because only that module was imported; no stub.
